- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1–2% above true peak or add lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model frequently underestimates downward moves — increase forecast sensitivity to recent low sentiment or add 0.5–1.0% buffer below true low.
- Model consistently underestimates true price declines in 30-day horizon — apply 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to forecast if recent 7-day average sentiment is negative.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., >+0.30), model often overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 14-day high or apply 0.5% downward correction.
- Forecast bias is strongest in early 30-day window — apply 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to first 5–7 days if sentiment is negative or volatile.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 within 5 days), model often fails to adjust — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days.
